newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: P&O Nedlloyd beef up Grand Alliance.
newsitem.headline: P&O Nedlloyd beef up Grand Alliance.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch shipping joint venture P&O Nedlloyd said on Tuesday it was opting to pursue its activities in an alliance with Hapag Lloyd, Nippon Yusen Kaisha and Neptune Orient Lines.

The 50-50 joint venture operated by Britain's P&O Containers and Dutch Royal Nedlloyd has functioned as a member of two rival alliances since the merger became effective on January 1, but this was not a long-term option, a Nedlloyd spokesman said.
"We have opted to go forward with our partners in the Grand Alliance, which will be improved and upgraded," he said.

Prior to the merger of the two companies' global container shipping activities, P&O had been a member of the Grand Alliance, while Nedlloyd formed part of the rival Global Alliance together with Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Orient Overseas Container Line and American President Lines.
P&O Nedlloyd said it had held "constructive discussions" with both alliances.
"The sound product, lower cost base and compatible building plans of the Grand (led us)...to conclude that the Grand was the correct way ahead," it said in a statement.
It said the new-look Grand Alliance was expected to be implemented in the first quarter of 1998.

"Our choice...will offer P&O Nedlloyd a most competitive service at the lowest cost base, particularly relating to ship systems and terminals," the statement quoted P&O Nedlloyd chief executive officer Tim Harris as saying.
